comment: The regression suite. Every statement this skill has ever parsed correctly lives here, so that a change to the shared library is checkable rather than hopeful. `file` is resolved against --root (default: the current directory); a case whose file is absent is SKIPPED, never failed - the statements are not redistributed with the skill, and some of them are private.

cases.name: BT
cases.shape: two columns, date carry-forward, repeating page header whose phone number lands in the debit band, four trailer rows past the last transaction

cases.name: Exim
cases.shape: three columns with a running balance to discard, dated continuation lines, negatives kept in their own column by the statement's own totals

cases.name: Unicredit
cases.shape: one signed column, eu numbers, two date columns, amounts inside the description

cases.name: UABank card
cases.shape: five numeric columns, Cyrillic headers, space thousands separator splitting numbers in two, transaction times on the row's second line

cases.name: demo sheet
cases.shape: csv, bands are column indices, a wrapped narrative row

cases.name: demo Dr/Cr
cases.shape: one unsigned column with the side in a marker column

cases.name: Unicredit (from scratch)
cases.shape: the same statement parsed with no ColumnSpec at all -- proof the suite checks output, not implementation
